newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks gain ground in early morning.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks gain ground in early morning.

text.p: Tokyo stocks gained ground in early morning trade on Wednesday, encouraged by a surge on Wall Street on Tuesday, brokers said.

After seven minutes of trade, the key 225-share Nikkei average had jumped 227.82 or 1.22 percent to 18,898.19. June Nikkei futures were bid-only at 18,830. The Japanese market was closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.
"The U.S. stock surge has erased one unclear factor that Tokyo has worried about," said Seiki Orimi, manager of stock information services at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
On Tuesday, the Dow industrials closed up 179 points or 2.65 percent at 6,962. It was the blue-chip index's second-largest point rise in a single day.
U.S. stocks rocketed higher as weaker-than-expected data on wage inflation and orders for manufactured goods soothed Wall Street's concerns over rising interest rates.
There had been fears in Tokyo that strong U.S. economic data might hit the Dow this week and that any sharp decline in U.S. stocks could damage Japanese stocks, brokers said.
